## Annotation

The BC section (heading “Choices for Supports in Independent Living”) states: “Initiated in 1994, the Choices for Supports in Independent Living program provides flexible self-directed home care for clients with chronic health conditions.” It says the program is supported by Spinal Cord Injury BC and the Individualized Funding Resource Centre, served 956 clients in 2015–16 (80 percent under age 65), and is administered through regional health authorities and funded by the Ministry of Health.

The title wording (“Choices for Supports”) differs from the ministry’s current “Choice in Supports.” Eligibility wording in the scan (chronic conditions, post-hospital, end-of-life) does not match the current provincial CSIL page’s high-physical-care-needs formula. Those mismatches are left as features of this secondary source, not corrected against the ministry page.

This is a 1994-side source in the founding-year conflict.

## Open questions

- Which informant or document supplied “Initiated in 1994.”
- Why the scan’s eligibility description diverges from the current HCC manual.
